parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by simple harmonic motion.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A block is suspended from a spring, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The block is pulled down and released at time *t* = 0. It then oscillates vertically with simple harmonic motion.

Fig. 4.2 shows the variation of the velocity *v* of the block with height *h* of the base of the block above the floor.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: Determine the amplitude, in cm, of the oscillations.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the angular frequency of the oscillations is 3.2 rad s⁻¹.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the period *T* of the oscillations.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
On Fig. 4.3, sketch the variation of *h* with time *t* from *t* = 0 to *t* = 6.0 s.

[[fig:f3]]

figures.caption: Fig. 4.1
figures.alt: A block hangs from a vertical spring attached to a support above a floor, with the height h marked between the block and floor.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.2
figures.alt: A velocity-versus-height graph shows an oval closed curve on a grid, with velocity v on the vertical axis and height h on the horizontal axis.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.3
figures.alt: A blank grid for sketching height h against time t, with h on the vertical axis and t on the horizontal axis.
